title: Setup
content:
# Welcome to SJB Writer

**Your stories. Your worlds. Your words.**

Every story begins somewhere. Maybe you have a character who will not leave you alone, a world waiting to be explored, or a plot that has been rattling around in your head for years. SJB Writer is here to help you bring those pieces together, keep your projects organized, and give your imagination room to work.

Whether you are building an epic fantasy, plotting a mystery, or finally tackling that novel you've been meaning to write, this is your workspace. Make it your own, work at your own pace, and keep your attention where it belongs: on the story.

## Before You Begin

SJB Writer organizes your work into a few essential parts. You do not need to configure everything before you start writing, but setting up the basics now will make your life easier later.

1. **Choose your project.** Create or select the project you want to work on. Each project has its own writing files and background material, keeping the details of one story separate from another.

2. **Add your background material.** Use the Background area for information you want to keep close at hand: character profiles, worldbuilding notes, timelines, research, and continuity details. Start with what you have. You can add more as your story grows.

3. **Explore your prompts.** Prompts help you tell your chosen AI model what you want it to do. Begin with a suitable existing prompt, or create your own when you are ready. You can refine these as you discover what works best for you.

4. **Set up your writing space.** Create or open a writing file and adjust the editor to suit your preferences. Your manuscript does not have to be planned from beginning to end before you type that first sentence.

That's all you need for now. You can build out your workspace as your project develops.

## Ready to Find Your Way Around?

Next up is **Getting Started**, where we will walk through the editor's basic navigation, explain what each pane on the left is there to do, and show how the pieces fit together.

You'll notice that this file, Setup, is named at the top of the Editor and highlighted on the left in the Project/Background panel. We'll talk more about both in the next lesson.

For now, look under Background for Writing. Click the arrow beside the 2 - Getting Started folder to expand it, then select 2.1 - Look Around to continue the tutorial.

Your next great story is waiting. Let's get to it!
